extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, librarians, folklorists, educators, and community members seeking to access or use Indigenous storytelling materials in the Library of Congress / American Folklife Center collections.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and resource listing for locating, accessing, and responsibly using Indigenous storytelling recordings, field notes, and related materials from the American Folklife Center collections for the US and Canada. Emphasizes restrictions, community consultation, provenance, language, and archival access procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access restrictions (seasonality/occasion/topic/teller/audience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the stories included are subject to restrictions based on seasonality, occasion, topic, teller, audience, or other criteria. The AFC works to ensure that access to these materials via its digital collections and onsite in the Reading Room is available only in accordance with these restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat recordings and texts as potentially restricted; before accessing or disseminating materials, determine what restrictions apply (seasonal/ceremonial stories, audience-limited tellings, teller-specific permissions). Follow AFC access controls for digital and onsite use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact tribal communities to ensure proper usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Please contact the tribal communities to which these stories and storytellers belong to ensure their proper usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to research, publication, performance, or other reuse, consult the relevant tribal community for guidance, permissions, and culturally appropriate handling. Community consultation is presented as a required step for proper use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative curation and community-authored contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ancestral Voices project is the result of a collaborative venture among the AFC, the Passamaquoddy Tribe of Maine, and the creators of TK Labels and Mukurtu CMS. Passamaquoddy elders have provided cultural narratives and added traditional knowledge about Passamaquoddy recordings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, undertake collaborative projects that involve tribal elders and community members in documenting, labeling, and contextualizing materials; use community-driven tools (e.g., TK Labels, Mukurtu) to represent Traditional Knowledge and access preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and document tribal approvals for transfers and stewardship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Zuni Tribal council and its governor... approved the transfer of the master tapes to the American Folklife Center in 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and respect records of tribal approvals or agreements governing collection transfers and custody. Ensure archival stewardship honors the terms under which materials were transferred or entrusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include provenance and performer attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections include field recordings, photographs, and notes by collectors and list storytellers and performers (names, dates, places, collectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using or citing materials, provide full provenance: collector, teller/performer names, tribal affiliation, date and place of recording, collection/call number. Accurate attribution supports ethical use and research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original language and provide accurate translations/transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings are often in Indigenous languages (e.g., Zuni, Tlingit, Southern Tutchone, Onondaga, Ottawa) and some manuscripts include interlineal translations in English or translations/explanations by the performer or collector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve recordings' original-language content and accompanying interlinear translations or field notes; when producing translations or transcripts, document translator, method, and any interpretive notes; avoid replacing or erasing linguistic/dialectal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and protect ceremonial and cultural protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: The recordings in this collection contain songs and stories on Tlingit history as well as ceremonial and cultural protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify material that embodies ceremonial/cultural protocol and treat it with special care—this may include restricted access, limited public dissemination, or requiring community permission for use. Do not present ceremonial material out of context or in ways that violate protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify performer/community status and consent for public programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions note performers who are enrolled members of specific Nations and who "regularly participate in tribal events," and indicate their performances and interviews were recorded at AFC public programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before using recordings in public programs or reproductions, verify the performer's community membership/status and that consent for public dissemination has been obtained; respect conditions the performer or community places on reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Library of Congress access and request procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Several items note "Request in the Jefferson or Adams Buildings Reading Rooms."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to LOC procedures for requesting and accessing materials (onsite reading room requests, call numbers). Understand that some items may not be digitized or may require in-person consultation under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contextual materials (field notes, interviews, introductions) to inform interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Many collections include field notes, transcripts, introductions, discussions, vocabulary, explanations, and/or translations by performers or collectors to accompany recordings and songs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on accompanying documentation (field notes, collector correspondence, interviews, introductions) to inform interpretation and presentation. Use contextual materials to avoid misinterpretation and to situate stories within cultural, historical, and ceremonial frameworks.
